pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. She is a sun.
   B. She is bright.
   C. She is as bright as the sun.
   D. She is a shining star.

2. Which is a part of an oral narrative? (1 mark)
   A. The ending
   B. A stamp
   C. A price tag
   D. A page number

3. In The farmer was weary after a long day in the shamba, weary means (1 mark)
   A. very rich
   B. very tired
   C. very hungry
   D. very loud

4. Why do we explain a proverb in our own words? (1 mark)
   A. To show we understand the lesson
   B. To make it longer
   C. To hide it
   D. To change it forever

5. How should you collect proverbs from an elder? (1 mark)
   A. Take it without asking
   B. Refuse to listen
   C. Greet politely and listen to the whole proverb
   D. Interrupt

6. What is an imaginative composition? (1 mark)
   A. A story made from the imagination
   B. A news report
   C. A list of prices
   D. A weather forecast

7. Which value should be shown in a market skit? (1 mark)
   A. Stealing
   B. Rudeness
   C. Honesty, such as giving correct change
   D. Cheating

8. What should you do if a classmate's story is not as good as yours? (1 mark)
   A. Interrupt
   B. Laugh at them
   C. Listen politely and give kind feedback
   D. Leave

9. What is skimming? (1 mark)
   A. Copying the text
   B. Reading backwards
   C. Reading quickly to get the main idea
   D. Reading slowly for every word

10. Which strategy would you use to find a price in an advert? (1 mark)
   A. Scanning
   B. Singing
   C. Drawing
   D. Skimming

11. Which group of words is a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. The customer pays fifty shillings.
   B. Pays fifty
   C. The customer in the market
   D. Fifty shillings

12. What does change mean in a shop? (1 mark)
   A. A journey
   B. The weather
   C. The clothes
   D. Money given back after paying

13. Where should the comma go in I have money and I want a book? (1 mark)
   A. After have
   B. After I
   C. Before and
   D. After want

14. Which is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. Elephant
   B. Lion
   C. Zebra
   D. Goat

15. What does it mean to advocate for animal welfare? (1 mark)
   A. To ignore them
   B. To hide them
   C. To harm animals
   D. To speak in support of caring for animals

16. The cow eats grass next to the river. Which word means the same as next to? (1 mark)
   A. inside
   B. under
   C. beside
   D. above

17. What should you do while a classmate recites? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Listen and respect them
   C. Leave
   D. Talk

18. How should you read a sad poem? (1 mark)
   A. Without a pause
   B. Fast and loudly
   C. Laughing
   D. Slowly and softly

19. What does a picture story use? (1 mark)
   A. Only numbers
   B. Only maps
   C. Pictures showing the beginning, middle and end
   D. Only names

20. What are the events of a story? (1 mark)
   A. The margin
   B. What happens step by step
   C. The title
   D. The author

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain when you would skim and when you would scan. Give one example of each. (5 marks)

22. Write a short story of five sentences that ends with the proverb A stitch in time saves nine. (5 marks)

23. Name three headings in a story plan. (3 marks)

24. Choose one proverb and explain its meaning. Then describe a real situation at school where it would apply. (5 marks)

25. Explain what a subject and a predicate are, then write one sentence and divide it. (5 marks)

26. Join with but: The trader was tired. He kept working. (3 marks)

27. Explain what an oral narrative is. (2 marks)

28. Explain the difference between skimming and scanning. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — She is as bright as the sun.
   It uses as to compare.

2. A — The ending
   Stories have openings, characters, events and endings.

3. B — very tired
   A long day of work suggests tiredness.

4. A — To show we understand the lesson
   Explaining shows understanding of the meaning.

5. C — Greet politely and listen to the whole proverb
   Politeness and careful listening are important.

6. A — A story made from the imagination
   Imaginative compositions are made-up stories.

7. C — Honesty, such as giving correct change
   Skits can show good values.

8. C — Listen politely and give kind feedback
   Respect is important.

9. C — Reading quickly to get the main idea
   Skimming gives the general idea.

10. A — Scanning
   You know exactly what you need.

11. A — The customer pays fifty shillings.
   It has a subject and a predicate.

12. D — Money given back after paying
   Change is the money you get back.

13. C — Before and
   A comma comes before the joining word.

14. D — Goat
   Goats are kept by people.

15. D — To speak in support of caring for animals
   Advocating means speaking in support.

16. C — beside
   Beside and next to both show the side.

17. B — Listen and respect them
   Good listeners respect performers.

18. D — Slowly and softly
   Slow and soft matches sadness.

19. C — Pictures showing the beginning, middle and end
   A picture story tells events with drawings.

20. B — What happens step by step
   Events are the actions in order.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: Skim when you want the main idea, for example looking through an article. Scan when you want one fact, for example looking for a name on a list.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two situations and two marks for examples and one mark for correct meaning.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five clear sentences with a beginning, problem, ending and the proverb used correctly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence up to four and one mark for using the proverb correctly.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each heading.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any correct proverb with a sensible meaning and a matching situation, for example A stitch in time saves nine means fix small problems early, such as mending a small tear in a uniform before it grows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the proverb, two marks for the meaning and two marks for a clear situation.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: The subject is who or what the sentence is about and the predicate says what the subject does. Example: The girl (subject) counts the coins (predicate).
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two meanings, one for a sentence, and two marks for the correct division.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: The trader was tired, but he kept working.
   Working / marking points: One mark for but, one for the comma, one for correct order.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: An oral narrative is a story told aloud, passed on from person to person, that entertains and teaches.
   Working / marking points: One mark for told aloud and one mark for entertain or teach.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Skimming is quick reading for the main idea and scanning is quick searching for a specific fact.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition.
